Subject: Post-call: Helix parallelism profile & provisional quota ask

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for the time this morning — great conversation on the chat use case and spike traffic pattern. Quick summary of the things we agreed to validate so we can move the pilot forward: 

1) Performance targets you called out
   - p95 latency target for short chat replies: <= 200 ms (end-to-end from request to first token)
   - sustained throughput target: ~120 concurrent request holders (avg session length ~35–50s)
   - peak bursts up to ~300 parallel requests for short windows (30–60s) during campaign sends
   - streaming requirements: SSE/websocket-style chunked responses, per-connection keep-alive

2) Data points we asked you to confirm (below) — please reply inline:
   - average request payload: ~150 tokens? (prompt+history)
   - average generated tokens per response: ~40–80 tokens
   - expected percentage of streaming vs non-streaming calls: ~70% streaming

3) Redwood provisional asks / next steps
   - I attached a short SLO worksheet (helix-slo-draft.xlsx) — can you fill the highlighted cells (avg tokens, peak QPS windows, number of persistent connections)?
   - For now, we can provision a pilot quota: recommended starting pool = 250 parallel request slots with a burst allowance of 400 for 30s windows while we validate latency.
   - Could you share procurement contact and PO time expectations so we can align on pilot start?

I'll loop in Marissa (solutions) and Karthik (infra) for a technical sizing note and a compact ratecard for the pilot.

Thanks —
Neha Kapoor

Neha — thanks for the recap, this matches our notes. Quick answers inline: 

- avg request payload: about 140–160 tokens (history pruned to last 3 turns)
- avg generated tokens: ~55 tokens
- streaming vs non-streaming: yes ~70% streaming, the rest are quick single-shot classification calls

Additional detail: we run a nightly campaign at 02:00 PST that historically creates a spike — recent runs produced ~320 concurrent requests for ~45 seconds; we can try to time a test during the pilot window.

Procurement: procurement@helixpay.com is our AP contact; PO process typically 2–3 weeks once pricing is agreed. Ideally we aim for a pilot kickoff the week of Jan 10, 2027.

One more question: what does Redwood recommend for connection pooling vs. persistent websocket count — we expect about 80 long-lived websocket sessions (customer service agents) plus the bursty API traffic.

—Alex

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Post-call: Helix parallelism profile & provisional quota ask — technical sizing note

Hi Alex / Neha —

Thanks for the context — below is a pragmatic pilot configuration and rationale. I kept it concise so your procurement team can see concrete numbers.

Pilot proposal (30-day):
- Concurrency pool (parallel request slots): 250 slots. Rationale: covers your sustained ~120 concurrent plus operational headroom and accounts for SSD/CPU/KV cache warmups during burst tests.
- Burst allowance: 400 concurrent slots for up to 45s windows. This matches the campaign spike you reported (~320) but adds buffer for measurement.
- Sustained QPS cap: 100 requests/sec (non-burst). With avg tokens (150 in) + 55 out, estimated token generation rate fits within a single dedicated ND instance cluster at this scale for the pilot.
- Connection model: support both HTTP/1.1 keep-alive and websocket/SSE. Recommended:
    * Max concurrent websocket sessions: 120 (you reported 80 long-lived sessions; we add 50% buffer).
    * Connection multiplexing: enable HTTP/2 multiplexing for client pools issuing many short requests — this reduces TCP socket usage for burst windows.
- Streaming specifics: Redwood streams tokens as they are generated. If you need strict first-byte p95 < 200ms, we'll prioritize low-latency instances and pre-warm KV cache for selected endpoints.

Rate limit policy (pilot):
- Default bucket: 100 QPS, token-bucket refill, per-api-key.
- Burst bucket: allows spikes up to 400 QPS for 30–60s windows; controlled with sliding-window enforcement to avoid long tail throttling.
- Connection-level limits: 6 concurrent requests per connection recommended for HTTP/2 clients; for single-connection websocket clients we don't enforce per-connection QPS but global per-api-key concurrency will apply.

Monitoring / SLA gating:
- We will instrument p50/p95/p99 latency for first token and completion.
- If p95 exceeds 250 ms over a 5-minute rolling window during the pilot, Redwood ops will throttle low-priority traffic and notify Helix for tuning.
- We'll share a compact pilot dashboard (token-level cost, latency breakdown, error rate) and a short runbook for escalation.

Next steps I can action:
- I attached a compact ratecard and a filled SLO worksheet (redwood-ratecard-compact.pdf & helix-slo-draft.xlsx).
- If these numbers look OK, Neha will draft an MAP with the pilot start window. For procurement, we can accept a signed PO or DocuSign agreement for the pilot.

If you want, we can also run a controlled spike test (internal load generation) during the first week to validate the burst policy and tune instance types.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Hi Neha / Marissa —

Thanks — this is very helpful and the numbers look reasonable for a pilot. A couple of quick items: 

1) Pilot start: we are targeting week of Jan 10, 2027. Procurement looped in (procurement@helixpay.com). PO lead time ~2 weeks after pricing agreement.
2) Please send a one-page MAP we can sign (dates, pilot capacity: 250 concurrency with 400 burst, basic ratecard, success criteria: p95 <= 250ms and error rate < 1% over a rolling 5-minute window).
3) We want a controlled spike test in week 1 to validate the burst policy — Marissa, can your team run that with our test account?

If you can get me a MAP and a DocuSign link this week, procurement will start the PO flow and we should be set to begin Jan 10.

—Alex
